title: Zephyrine and the Autopsy
premise: Ada Marchetti, a retired detective turned failing bookseller, is paid an absurd retainer by a nervous stranger to prove that Zephyrine Voss — the town's beloved matriarch — will not be murdered at the upcoming anniversary dinner. When Ada finds evidence the 'future' murder has already been staged once, twenty years ago, and covered up by the very people who raised her, she realizes the client is Zephyrine's presumed-dead twin, kept hidden to protect an inheritance built on a death. As the anniversary dinner approaches, Ada must locate the living witness everyone swears is dead and decide whether exposing the town's founding lie will save her or destroy the only belonging she's ever had. In the end, the truth comes out at the dinner table itself: Zephyrine confesses, the inheritance is dissolved, and Ada chooses the bookshop — and the town — over the badge she buried.
about_author: August Thornbury is the pen name of a former small-town coroner's assistant who spent a decade cataloguing other people's endings before turning to fiction. They live above a secondhand bookshop and insist every mystery they write begins with something someone refused to bury.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Ada Marchetti's POV. A gaunt stranger named Corin leaves a thick envelope on the counter of Marchetti & Sons Books, asking her to prove a murder will not happen — then vanishes before she can refuse. The retainer is triple what the shop owes. Beat: reluctant curiosity masking old hunger for purpose.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She canvasses her mental index of Harbor Glen's residents for the name Zephyrine Voss and learns the anniversary dinner for the Voss cannery fortune is six weeks away. Her deputy-sheriff ex-partner Ruiz warns her off unpaid ghosts. Beat: the comfort of routine beginning to crack.

chapters.title: A House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Posing as an appraiser, Ada tours Voss House and notices a locked servants' wing preserved like a shrine — dust sheets, untouched, but recently vacuumed. Someone still tends a room no one admits exists. Beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Corin's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Corin watches Ada from across the street, revealing to the reader he knows the shop, the town, and Ada herself intimately — though not why. He leaves a second envelope containing a photograph of two identical girls, 1968. Beat: dread braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Twin in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the historical society archives Ada finds one twin listed as born and dead the same week: 'Zephyrine II.' The surviving sister inherited everything. The death certificate bears the signature of Ada's own late mentor, Doc Halloran. Beat: betrayal surfacing through paper.

chapters.title: What Doc Halloran Kept
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Searching her mentor's sealed effects, Ada finds his private casebook: a page torn out, but an index entry reading 'Voss — see me before you file.' The omission was deliberate, protective, hers to inherit. Beat: grief complicated by complicity.

chapters.title: Dinner Invitations
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Voss's POV. The matriarch prepares her guest list for the sixtieth anniversary dinner, crossing out names and adding one in fresh ink: 'A. Marchetti.' She knows someone is asking questions. Beat: elegant menace; the hunter aware of being hunted.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Is Dead
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Everyone points Ada to the one person who could confirm the twin swap — groundskeeper Milo Fen, dead eleven years. But his pension checks were cashed last month. Beat: hope rekindling inside suspicion.

chapters.title: Salt and Smoke
chapters.summary: Ruiz's POV. Ruiz quietly reopens a cold file after finding Ada's fingerprints on archive boxes, torn between loyalty and duty. He discovers the original 1968 autopsy report was signed but never filed. Beat: institutional rot seen through a decent man's eyes.

chapters.title: The Room Behind the Dust Sheets
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada breaks into the preserved servants' wing and finds a child's bedroom, a girl's clothing in adult sizes, and letters addressed to 'Z' from someone signing 'C.' Corin has been here too — the vacuum tracks are his. Beat: intimacy with a stranger's secret.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine rehearses her toast, poisons nothing yet, but sets two place settings where protocol demands one. Flashbacks reveal the night she let her sister be declared dead to escape their father. Beat: sympathy curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Cash and Consequence
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The shop's landlord suddenly forgives three months' rent; the historical society burns its loan records. Someone with money is erasing Ada's trail in both directions. Beat: paranoia — every kindness now reads as a bribe.

chapters.title: Milo Fen, Alive and Angry
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the pension payments, Ada finds Milo living under another name upcoast. He confirms the swap: the first Zephyrine died of their father's violence; the survivor took her identity to inherit and end him. The witness everyone swears is dead is Milo himself. Beat: the truth arriving smaller and sadder than expected.

chapters.title: Why Corin Came to Me
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Corin reveals he is the son of the dead twin — raised abroad on trust-fund silence, hired by Zephyrine herself to test whether the town could survive the truth. He chose Ada because Doc Halloran trusted her. Beat: the client becomes the confession.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine confronts Corin privately, offering him the inheritance whole if he leaves before the dinner. He asks instead for his mother's name spoken aloud. She cannot say it. Beat: the theme made flesh — survival bought with silence.

chapters.title: Ruiz Makes His Choice
chapters.summary: Ruiz's POV. With the unfiled autopsy in hand, Ruiz must arrest Ada for obstruction or stand with her. He files nothing, brings coffee instead, and says, 'Twenty years I wondered why you quit.' Beat: alliance forged in shared compromise.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada lays out the evidence like a hand of cards: certificate, casebook, letters, Milo's statement. She drafts her resignation from the town itself, unsure which side of the door she'll sleep on tomorrow. Beat: quiet dread before the storm.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Sixty years of Harbor Glen gather under chandeliers. Zephyrine rises to toast, sees Ada seated where Corin should be, and understands the trap is mutual. Beat: held breath; civility stretched to tearing.

chapters.title: A Toast to the Dead
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Mid-toast, Ada stands and tells the room about the girl born and buried in the same week. Glasses freeze. Zephyrine does not deny it — she finishes the toast to her sister's memory instead. Beat: climax; the truth detonating softly.

chapters.title: Confession at the Head of the Table
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine confesses fully: the death, the cover-up, the decades of tending the locked room. She surrenders the inheritance to a trust in her sister's name and asks the town to remember both girls. Beat: catharsis without absolution.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Filed Under M
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later: indictments for the old cover-up, Milo testifying under his real name, Corin staying on to restore the servants' wing as a memorial. Ada declines to reopen her detective license. Beat: bittersweet settling.

chapters.title: Open for Business
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Spring. The bookshop thrives on notoriety it never asked for. Corin pays his final invoice with a framed photograph of the two girls, hung behind the register. Ada alphabetizes a new shelf: local history, finally told whole. Beat: belonging earned, inheritance redefined.
